info.title: Calimero node API
info.description:
Every route a `merod` node serves, on one HTTP API at its `--listen` address. The route table is `router` in `crates/node/src/api.rs`; this document is generated from the registry next to it (`crates/node/src/api/openapi.rs`), whose tests hold it to that table.

**Requests are sealed.** Only `GET /health` and `GET /attestation` travel in the clear. Every other request goes inside the sealed channel (`calimero-sealed`, wire format v2, Noise NK) to the transport key the node's attestation binds, after the client checked the quote against a mero-tee release it trusts; a TDX node refuses plain requests (a node started with `--dev` accepts them). A generic HTTP tool (curl, Postman, a generated client) therefore reaches only those two routes: use a sealing client (`meroctl`, `calimero-client` for Rust, mero-js `CalimeroClient`, calimero-client-py `CloudClient`), or put such a client's transport under the generated code. The paths, bodies and answers below are what travels inside the channel.

**Errors** answer `{ status, error, message, details? }`: `error` is the code, `details` says more (the challenge of a `412 CONFIRM_REQUIRED`, the statement of a `428 OPERATOR_SIGNATURE_REQUIRED`, `leaderUrl` of a `421 NOT_LEADER`). Each operation lists the codes it raises itself and those its credential implies, per status in `x-calimero-codes` (every error answer is the one `Error` schema); any operation may also answer `400 BAD_REQUEST`, `400 REJECTED`, `421 NOT_LEADER` and `503 UNAVAILABLE`. A route that takes a session may answer `421 WRONG_NODE` (no `details`): try another node. `x-calimero-details` on an error response maps each of its codes that carries `details` to that value's schema, and `x-calimero-error-details` at the root maps every such code: one code, one schema, so a client reads `details` by `error`.

**Retries.** `x-calimero-retry-safe` marks the operations a client may send again after a `503` or a lost answer (`x-calimero-retry-requires` names the body field that makes it so, an idempotency key). The sealed channel's own `503` (`{ error: { code: "busy", message } }`, outside the envelope: too many sealed requests or sessions at once; the schema `x-calimero-sealed-refusal` names) carries `Retry-After: 1` on any sealed route; the node's `503 UNAVAILABLE` answers carry none. `x-calimero-step-up` (with `x-calimero-user-verification`, and `x-calimero-step-up-when` where it applies only sometimes) and `x-calimero-operator` mark the two-round operations below.

**Numbers** that may exceed 2^53 (fuel, bytes) travel as decimal strings (D20); every other integer is `format: int64` (read it into a 64-bit integer), and stays below 2^53.

details.description: Free-form JSON: its shape is not this API's (see the description around it for whose it is).

Error.description: An error answer: `error` is the code. `details`, absent for most codes, has the schema `x-calimero-details` names for the code on the operation's response (every code's: `x-calimero-error-details` at the document's root); a code it names no schema for carries none, or a value clients need not read.

Confirm.description: A passkey assertion over the challenge a `412 CONFIRM_REQUIRED` named: the same request sent again with it approves exactly that request.

ConfirmRequired.description: `details` of a `412 CONFIRM_REQUIRED`: the WebAuthn challenge to sign under `rpId` with one of the passkeys `allowCredentials` names (credential ids; empty: any of the account's), and the `challengeId` the retry's `confirm` names. `apps`: deleting a team that holds apps, the apps that go with it.

OperatorProof.description: The operator key's Ed25519 signature (hex) over the statement a `428 OPERATOR_SIGNATURE_REQUIRED` named, with that statement's nonce.

OperatorSignatureRequired.description: `details` of a `428 OPERATOR_SIGNATURE_REQUIRED`: the statement to sign (`args` is the JSON text of its arguments, as signed) and the exact bytes to sign (`message`, standard base64).

Assertion.description: The browser's answer to `navigator.credentials.get`, each field base64url.

Registration.description: The browser's answer to `navigator.credentials.create`, each field base64url.

Session.description: A session: its token (15 minutes, by the issuing node) and the refresh token for `/auth/refresh`.

error.description: Free-form JSON: its shape is not this API's (see the description around it for whose it is).

Applied.description: An entry an app's log applied: its index, how it ended and the app's error (`null` when it ended `ok`; the app's own error value otherwise, free-form). `details` of a `422 UPGRADE_FAILED`.

NotLeader.description: `details` of a `421 NOT_LEADER`: the leader's URL to send the same request to, and its node id where known.

FeatureNotActive.description: `details` of a `409 FEATURE_NOT_ACTIVE`: the feature the request needs, the cluster version it ships in (`needs`) and the version active now (`null`: none logged, and the nodes could not say).

RuntimeTooOld.description: `details` of a `409 RUNTIME_TOO_OLD`: the runtime the release needs and the replicas known to fall short of it, each with what it runs (a version, or `{ before }`: a release older than that one).

ReleaseDeadline.description: `details` of a `409 RELEASE_DEADLINE`: the mero-tee release whose deadline passed, and the deadline (`after` RFC 3339, `afterSecs` Unix seconds). Approving that release (or a newer one) lifts it.

UpgradePending.description: `details` of a `409 UPGRADE_PENDING`: the release every node must run first, and the nodes that run an older one (`release` `null`: one this node could not attest).

fields.description: Free-form JSON: its shape is not this API's (see the description around it for whose it is).

AppError.description: `details` of a `422 APP_ERROR`: the app's error code, its fields (the app's own value, free-form: the object its ABI declares for the error, or the app's message as a string when that is not JSON), and the log index of the call (absent when the node refused it before it ran: `UnknownMethod`, `WrongKind`, `Forbidden`, `ConfirmNotAView`, `NotAView`, `ConfirmRequired`).

Trap.description: `details` of a `422 TRAP`: the log index of the run, how it trapped, and the engine's account of it.

error.description: Free-form JSON: its shape is not this API's (see the description around it for whose it is).

InitFailed.description: `details` of a `422 INIT_FAILED`: the app made, and the error its `init` ended with (the app log's, free-form).

RecoveryNotReady.description: `details` of a `409 RECOVERY_NOT_READY`: when the recovery may finish (Unix seconds).

UploadPosition.description: `details` of a `409 PART_CONFLICT`, `409 PART_OUT_OF_ORDER` or `409 UPLOAD_INCOMPLETE`: the part the upload expects next.

RetryAfter.description: `details` of a `503 TIMEOUT` or `503 FILES_UNAVAILABLE`: the seconds to wait before sending the same request (with the same idempotency key) again.

ServiceRefused.description: `details` of a `400 UNSUPPORTED_BUNDLE`, `400 BAD_BUNDLE` or `400 COMPUTE_ABI_MISMATCH` refusing one service of a release: the service, and `compute: true` when it was that service's compute component. Absent when the refusal is of a raw bundle.

SealedRefusal.description: The sealed channel's own refusal, outside the envelope and in the clear: not an `Error`. `busy` (`503`, with `Retry-After: 1`): too many sealed requests or sessions at once, send it again; the other codes (`400`, `malformed` and the like) say the envelope could not be opened.

Receipt.description: The answering node's signature (receipt key, hex) over `(app, index, SHA-256(JCS(result)), node)`.

Access.description: Who may reach an app at all.

OrgRole.description: A member's role in an organization.

TeamRole.description: A member's standing in one team.

TeamJoin.description: Open (`everyone` who reaches the parent) or restricted (`invite`) membership.

OutboundSelection.description: `manifest` (every prefix the release declares) or these prefixes.

Page.description: A page of a list: `next` is the `after` of the next page, `null` on the last.

AttestationDoc.description: A node's attestation: the TDX quote (base64), the key it binds (hex) and what it was asked for. `receiptKey` and `governance` with `purpose=receipts`, `kms` with `purpose=kms` on a node with a KMS record, `clusterIdentity` with `purpose=orchestrator`; `jobKey` only from a job node, never from this API.

KmsKeys.description: What a node verified of the mero-kms replicas it took its keys from: the storage key `merod` fetched, and the data disk's key the boot script fetched; each absent without a record.

KmsEvidence.description: The KMS quote a node accepted a key under: the KMS host, the mero-kms release (and image profile) whose signed policy it matched, the quote's registers (hex), its TCB status, SHA-256 and when it was verified (Unix seconds); `mock` (absent: false) in development builds only.

GroupStatus.description: A Raft group's status as one node sees it: the leader (`null`: none known), whether this node is it, the term, the last log index (`null`: an empty log), the applied index, and the voters and learners.

RollbackStatus.description: A node's rollback counter: the cluster's epoch (rollbacks forced so far), its generation and mark, whether this start was forced (`--accept-rollback`), and the seconds since mero-kms last acknowledged a checkpoint.

NodeRole.description: What a node does: hold app replicas, or run compute jobs.

NodeRecord.description: A registered node: its id, address, zone, role and (a job node's) compute pool, absent for none.

Quotas.description: The per-account limits, and the compute and file limits of each organization (or personal account) that has no override. `maxFuelPerDeveloperPerDay` (0: no limit) is a decimal string; the others are JSON numbers.

computeFuel.description: an unsigned 64-bit integer as a decimal string (D20)

OrgQuotas.description: One payer's limits in place of the cluster's; a limit left out is the cluster's.

maxFuelPerDeveloperPerDay.description: an unsigned 64-bit integer as a decimal string (D20)

QuotaSettings.description: `GET /ops/quotas`: the cluster's limits and, under `orgs`, each payer's overrides by payer id.

runs.description: an unsigned 64-bit integer as a decimal string (D20)

fuel.description: an unsigned 64-bit integer as a decimal string (D20)

wallMs.description: an unsigned 64-bit integer as a decimal string (D20)

writes.description: an unsigned 64-bit integer as a decimal string (D20)

bytesWritten.description: an unsigned 64-bit integer as a decimal string (D20)

events.description: an unsigned 64-bit integer as a decimal string (D20)

UsageDay.description: What an app's runs used on one UTC day (`date`, `YYYY-MM-DD`), each figure a decimal string; `wallMs` is information only.

RunFile.description: A file a run reads or wrote: its id, and its plaintext size and SHA-256 (hex) only for a caller who may list the app's files.

Run.description: A compute run's record, without its arguments or keys: its method, state, caps (`fuel` a JSON number here), inputs, attempts (`tsMs` Unix milliseconds) and final outcome (`null` while it runs; `message` the failure text, `null` unless the caller may list the app's files). `progress` is the leader's last poll (`null` elsewhere, when it is not active, or to a caller who may not list files); `queue` where the run waits for a job node, to a caller who may list files only.

AccountProof.description: A statement, signed with the answering node's receipt key (hex, Ed25519 over the statement's canonical JSON after its domain), that the account asked to bind `nonce` for `audience`, valid from `issuedAt` to `expiresAt` (Unix seconds).

AccountStatement.description: What an account proof states: the cluster and node, the account, the nonce and audience it binds, and when it was issued and expires (Unix seconds).

PackageOrigin.description: A custom frontend origin of a package: the rp-id its passkeys use, who registered it and when (RFC 3339), and whether the cluster serves the package's frontend there.

SignUpState.description: The sign-up policy and what it implies: whether organization invites and cluster sign-up invites admit a new account, and whether one is required.

ApprovedReleases.description: The mero-tee releases the scope approves now, after the change.

OutboundApproved.description: The outbound approval the scope holds now for the package's publisher (`signer`), after the change.

Deadlines.description: Every release deadline after the change, oldest release first (`after` RFC 3339, `afterSecs` Unix seconds).

SignUpSet.description: The cluster's governance and sign-up policy after the change.

InviteKey.description: The key of the cluster sign-up invite withdrawn.

UpgradeRun.description: An organization-wide upgrade run: the apps it targets, those done, and why each failed one failed.

initArgs.description: Free-form JSON: its shape is not this API's (see the description around it for whose it is).

metadata.description: Free-form JSON: its shape is not this API's (see the description around it for whose it is).

App.description: An app instance (a context) as the directory records it. `executor` is absent for an SDK 0.12 app (wasmer), which this node lists but does not run; `release` is the package release it runs, absent for a record from before or a raw upload; `restore` is a restore from a backup under way.

AppEntry.description: An app as `GET /apps` lists it: `package` and `version` name the release its bundle came from (`null` for a raw upload), `deployment` the deployment it was created from (`null` for none; absent from an older node, as 1.0.0-rc.1).

PackageRef.description: One service of one package release: `service` is absent for a single-service bundle, `compute` (absent: false) marks the service's compute component.

error.description: Free-form JSON: its shape is not this API's (see the description around it for whose it is).

Upgrade.description: The last upgrade tried on an app, done or failed: `from` and `to` are bundle hashes, `by` the account (or `operator`), `run` the organization-wide run it was part of, `apiKey` the upgrade key that made it.

metadata.description: Free-form JSON: its shape is not this API's (see the description around it for whose it is).

Package.description: A package and the releases of it the caller may see, oldest first; `latest` is the newest of those.

ApiKey.description: An API key as the account's list shows it (never its secret): `apps` and `methods` are `null` for every one; `upgrades` makes it an upgrade key.

metadata.description: Free-form JSON: its shape is not this API's (see the description around it for whose it is).

Org.description: An organization as `GET /orgs/{org}` answers it. `members` maps each account to its role, `capabilities` and `defaultCapabilities` are capability bits, `outboundApprovals` is keyed by package signer, `upgradeRuns` by run id; `recovery` is absent when the organization set no recovery key, `allApps` when no member gets every app added later.

metadata.description: Free-form JSON: its shape is not this API's (see the description around it for whose it is).

Team.description: A team as its organization records it: `members` maps each direct row to whether it is a lead; `capabilities` are capability bits per row; `defaultCapabilities` is absent when unset.

metadata.description: Free-form JSON: its shape is not this API's (see the description around it for whose it is).

TeamView.description: A team as `GET /orgs/{org}/teams/{team}` answers it: each member's row, the child teams the caller sees, its apps, and the caller's own row (`myRole`, `null` for none) and membership (`member`). `package` names the package of an app team; it and `defaultCapabilities` are absent from an older node (1.0.0-rc.1 sends neither).

Deployment.description: A deployment as its managers list it. `host` is its frontend host, `null` on a node with no apps domain; times are RFC 3339.

DeadLetter.description: A cross-app call that was never delivered: its sequence number, the target app and method, why, and when (`atMs`, Unix milliseconds).

Governance.description: Who decides what on this cluster: release approvals, app upgrades and outbound approvals (`owner`: each app's owner; `operator`: the operator), and, left out at their defaults, `deployments` (`open`), `deployers` (`operator`) and `signUp` (`open`).

OutboundApproval.description: What an owner approved for one publisher's apps to call out to: the approved URL prefixes, and every prefix it was shown.

AppScope.description: The scope whose approvals cover an app: its organization, or its owner's account (never named).

ClusterRelease.description: A mero-tee release the cluster's nodes run: how many run it, and whether the scope approved it (`true` where nothing was ever recorded).

BundleRelease.description: A bundle by its digest, with the release it came from where the reader may see it.

error.description: Free-form JSON: its shape is not this API's (see the description around it for whose it is).

ReportUpgrade.description: An app's last upgrade as a report shows it. `actor`, `error`, `run` and `apiKey` are shown to the app's people, never to the operator.

ReportApp.description: One app in a release report (`GET /auth/apps`, `GET /orgs/{org}/apps`, `GET /ops/apps`): its bundle and release (`package`, `null` where the reader may not see it), the publisher's key and bound organization, who holds its upgrades and release approvals, its last upgrade, the releases approved to hold it (`null`: unrestricted), each replica's release, and `lastWriteAt` (Unix seconds, `null` when unknown). `name`, `team`, `availableVersions` (newer releases, oldest first), `latestReachable` and `latestBlocked` (the newest release and why an upgrade would not take it) are for the app's people, never the operator.

DeploymentRecord.description: A deployment as the directory records it: the release it offers by app name (`addedAt` Unix seconds), who created it and when (Unix seconds).

DeployerGrant.description: A grant to install where deployments are granted: until when (Unix seconds; absent: it does not end), when and by whom it was granted.

SignUpInvite.description: A cluster sign-up invite, never its token: uses left, when it expires (`expiresAt` RFC 3339, `expiresAtSecs` Unix seconds), who made it and when (RFC 3339).

ProofOnly.description: What an operator decision that names nothing in its body may carry: none at first, the operator's proof after the `428`.

ConfirmOnly.description: The body of a step-up that names nothing else: none (or `{}`) at first, the passkey assertion after the `412`.

orgs.description: Free-form JSON: its shape is not this API's (see the description around it for whose it is).

maxFuelPerDeveloperPerDay.description: an unsigned 64-bit integer as a decimal string (D20)

computeFuel.description: an unsigned 64-bit integer as a decimal string (D20)

QuotaChanges.description: The limits `POST /ops/quotas` changes, each optional: without `org`, the cluster's (those `GET /ops/quotas` answers, `maxFuelPerDeveloperPerDay` a decimal string); with `org`, one payer's (`maxConcurrentRuns`, `computeFuel` a decimal string, `maxFileBytes`; `null` clears one). `orgs` is ignored. Any other property is refused `400 UNKNOWN_QUOTA`.

session.description: A passkey session's token (15 minutes, by the issuing node), from a passkey ceremony or `/auth/refresh`.

apiKey.description: An API key from `POST /auth/apikeys`, scoped to apps, methods and read-only as made.
